Where does collagen go after you drink it? Collagen supplements don't travel intact from your stomach straight to your skin or joints. Your digestive system breaks collagen down into smaller components, including amino acids and peptides, which are then absorbed and used by the body. Collagen is particularly rich in amino acids such as glycine and proline, which are among the building blocks involved in protein and collagen production. Vitamin C also plays an important role in normal collagen formation. Research has also explored whether certain collagen peptides may have signaling effects, so the story isn't simply “collagen gets destroyed.” The bigger takeaway? You're supplying raw materials, not shipping finished collagen directly to your skin. 💬 What benefit are you hoping to get from collagen? #collagen #collagenpeptides #collagenpowder #vitaminc #glycine #proline #protein #aminoacids #skinhealth #jointhealth #supplements #nutritiontok

Okay, so here’s the whole story. 👇 Three years. $39.90 a month. A scoop of multi-collagen in my coffee every single morning. Why? Because everyone I knew was on it, and it made total sense: you stop making as much collagen as you age, so you put it back. Right? Well. I finally checked. 📌 The skin studies: A 2025 review in the American Journal of Medicine pooled 23 trials with almost 1,500 people. Put them all together and skin looked better. But split them by who paid for them, and the trials the makers funded found benefits. The ones nobody in the industry paid for found nothing. The industry argues with how the studies were sorted, and that’s fair to know. Weigh it for yourself. Your mirror is data too. 📌 “Replacing what you’re losing”: It doesn’t go straight to your face. Your body breaks collagen down into small pieces first. Some of those pieces reach your blood, and then your body decides where they go. 📌 “Five types in one scoop”: I couldn’t find a single study showing a five-type blend beats plain collagen. The types mostly matter on the label. 📌 Hair and nails: For nails I found one small study of 25 women, with no comparison group, tied to the ingredient’s maker. The results looked good. For hair, I couldn’t find a collagen-only study at all. 📌 The one that surprised me: UC-II is a different thing entirely. It’s a tiny dose that works through your gut’s immune system, and it has a real trial behind it, for knees. Joints, not wrinkles. So I stopped the multi-collagen. Didn’t notice a thing. Three years, and I never once asked if it was working. That’s why I built PeptaVive. You tell it what you take, it shows you what the research actually says and who paid for it, and you decide. Then it helps you find out if it’s working for you. Keep it or drop it. 💛 What’s in your cabinet right now that you’ve never asked about?
